source.title: Bayesian Wind Tunnels for Model Selection
source.authors: Siddhartha R. Dalal; Vishal Misra; Abhay Parekh

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses grokking and reports delayed emergence of model-selection behavior, but does not test delayed train/test generalization as specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported grokking-like result measures Bayesian model-selection behavior, not training accuracy, test accuracy, or generalization after overfitting. It does not test whether smaller training sets take longer to generalize. The paper's references to grokking results from other work are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study trains transformers on synthetic in-context Bayesian model-selection tasks with on-the-fly data, so there is no fixed training set, no train/test split and no memorization-then-generalization gap. The 80K-step plateau then sudden emergence on rotations (single run) is a loss/capability plateau, not grokking as V1–V7 define it. No training-set-size sweep, weight decay, circuit tracking, initialization scale, LLM training or optimizer/numerical controls bear on any version. The grokking discussion is interpretive.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call the rotation dynamics 'grokking-style' and interpret them as circuit consolidation for a global algebraic relationship, while involution detection fits attention-based matching and learns smoothly. They flag that the transition comes from a single run and that the mechanism is an untested hypothesis. The paper's main conclusions concern Bayesian model selection and a perceptual-access boundary, not grokking.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains transformers on synthetic Bayesian model-selection tasks and tracks predictive entropy and inferred class posteriors, rather than testing training-versus-test accuracy on the grokking setups.
record.method_sensitivity: For the rotation model-selection task, curriculum annealing from π = 0.95 to 0.5 over 30K warmup steps accelerates convergence by ∼5× relative to no curriculum.

fits_no_version.finding: Without curriculum, a 2.8M transformer learning rotation-vs-bijection model selection shows an 80K-step plateau before sudden emergence (single run). A π-annealing curriculum speeds convergence ∼5×, while involution model selection learns smoothly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context capabilities that require arithmetic circuits on streamed synthetic data can show plateau-then-sudden-emergence dynamics, while relational ones learn smoothly; curriculum shortens the plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: An opaque-token rotation model trained 500K steps shows no late improvement (MAE flat from step 10K).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extended training does not produce late emergence when the task's discriminative statistic is not learnable under the encoding.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say they plan to release the code and evaluation harnesses.
record.problems: The delayed rotation transition is characterized from a single representative run, and the authors say a multi-seed characterization is future work. The reported metric is model-selection entropy rather than training/test accuracy, and the experiments do not test training-set-size dependence.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because the other reported metrics concern Bayesian model-selection accuracy or calibration, not delayed train/test generalization. Cited grokking results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: No fixed train set, no train/test accuracy, no dataset-size dependence of the delay.
No circuit or progress measure is tracked across the plateau; the induction-head account is explicitly untested.
No non-algorithmic data, no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
The frontier LLMs are probed zero-shot, with no training dynamics.
No weight-decay variation, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer or precision controls on the plateau.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification is confirmed. The paper cites the original sources, Power et al. and Nanda et al., only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training accuracy, test accuracy, chance-level test accuracy, overfitting, or a sweep over training-set size.
No generalizing circuit is measured or tracked, no memorizing component is removed, and no circuit-level progress measure is shown to anticipate a test-accuracy jump.
The reported experiments use synthetic algorithmic tasks; they do not test non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm transitions.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested for delayed generalization.
The paper does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias as an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The paper does not identify and compare algorithms learned across runs in the sense specified by this version.
The paper does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts produce and explain the claimed delayed generalization.

rows.subject: 2.8M-parameter transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on rotation-vs-bijection model-selection sequences without curriculum learning.
rows.value: 80K steps of plateau followed by sudden emergence of model selection
rows.uncertainty: not stated; characterized from a single representative run
rows.note: This is a grokking-like transition in model-selection behavior, not a reported training/test accuracy or generalization transition.
rows.check: On-the-fly data means training accuracy never saturates on a fixed set, so this is a plateau in in-context capability, not delayed generalization. Single run, no figure or numbers beyond '80K steps'.

rows.subject: 2.8M-parameter transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on rotation-vs-bijection model-selection sequences with curriculum annealing.

conditions.value: anneal π from 0.95 to 0.5 over 30K warmup steps

rows.measure: Time to convergence of model-selection behavior
rows.note: The acceleration concerns model-selection convergence, not time to generalization or a training-set-size comparison.
rows.check: Curriculum over the class prior π is a data-distribution choice, not a training-regime knob named in V3/V5/V7. '∼5×' has no absolute times reported.

rows.subject: Involution model
rows.operation_detail: Train on the involution-vs-bijection task and track entropy MAE.
rows.value: MAE is 0.058 at step 10K and improves steadily to 0.011 by step 230K
rows.note: The paper contrasts smooth learning of model-selection behavior with the rotation-task plateau; it does not report train/test generalization accuracy.
rows.check: Smooth MAE trajectory on the involution task. Valid as a contrast, but no versions are linked.

rows.subject: 25M-parameter opaque rotation model
rows.operation_detail: Extend training on the opaque rotation model-selection task.
rows.value: Remains flat at 1.28 bits from step 10,000 onward
rows.note: The paper reports no late improvement in this model-selection metric; this is not a test of delayed test-accuracy generalization.
rows.check: Extended-training control on a failed task, run to rule out late emergence. The 'flat at 1.28 bits' value is reported for the 25M model while 1.20 bits is reported elsewhere for 25M; this is a minor inconsistency in the source. The integer-model improvement (0.167→0.097) is omitted but also bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
